question.:question/problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\sqrt{84+3x}$ at the point where $x=-1.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=84+3x.$ Then $y=\sqrt{u}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot (3) \\  & =\frac{3}{2\sqrt{84+3x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $x=-1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=-1} & ={(\frac{3}{2\sqrt{84+3x}})|}_{x=-1} \\  & =\frac{3}{2\sqrt{84+3(-1)}} \\  & =\frac{3}{2\sqrt{81}} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$
